verdictRationale: The Writer closed the round-one severe issues with enforceable invariants: content-bound approval, strict reviewer sandboxing, and checksum-based install/update conflict semantics. The remaining safety boundaries around paths, dedupe, external sources, and legacy roots are now specific enough to drive implementation and test design without inventing major runtime policy.

falsifiability.failureCondition: An approved proposal is mutated after approval and then successfully promoted without creating a fresh approval record for the new content.
falsifiability.observableSignal: A draft artifact appears even though the proposal content hash, validation hash, target, or control-plane hash differs from the approval record.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Create a temp installed root, apply a valid proposal, approve it, edit its evidence or validation plan, then run promote and inspect exit code plus drafts directory contents.
falsifiability.threshold: promote must exit nonzero and create zero draft files

ledgerReview.rationale: Approval is now bound to proposal content hash, validation hash, target, and control-plane hash, with promote-time recomputation and mutation invalidation.
The model reviewer is explicitly data-only, denied write-capable tools, and disabled when that sandbox cannot be enforced.
Managed-template checksums, merge policies, conflict outputs, and manual-only files define non-overwrite update behavior.
The scoring rubric now maps each dimension to concrete bands and preserves threshold meaning across implementations.
The path invariant now requires code-owned root-relative paths, realpath checks, traversal rejection, symlink rejection, and same-directory atomic writes.
Proposal mutation now has explicit approved-content boundaries, per-proposal locks, lock timeout behavior, and atomic write requirements.
External sources now require explicit config records and credential references are barred from evidence, prompts, reports, proposals, approvals, and drafts.
The spec normalizes canonical harness/shared_factory paths and adds an acceptance check banning writes to legacy top-level shared_factory paths.

preserveList.summary: The v1 boundary remains appropriately conservative: reports, proposals, approvals, and drafts are allowed, while live shared artifact mutation is excluded.
The spec preserves the useful Hermes ideas without copying direct mutation, especially sidecar telemetry and separate deterministic versus model recommendations.
preserveList.lineRef: Sidecar Telemetry Contract / Model Review Sandbox

preserveList.summary: The validation plan is strong enough to catch the most likely unsafe-write, stale-approval, secret-leak, and scheduler-failure regressions.
